messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate observed for inference endpoints in us-west-2a (node-group: infer-g5-usw2a). Error pattern: TCP RST / connection timeouts egress -> internet/NAT (detected 03:14 UTC). Auto-escalating to #incidents.
emily: ack, I'm oncall. paging now. gathering logs.
emily: quick note: alerts show spike started at 03:13 UTC, p50 latency +150ms, 5xxs ~12% for last 2m.
ranjit: i'm pulling ENI metrics and host network qdisc stats. can someone run quick curl to one failing endpoint and paste output?
maria: ran a curl from inside a pod -> `curl -v https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate` -> `* Connection timed out` then `* Failed to receive HTTP response`.
dan: same from prow runner, `connect: connection reset by peer`.
emily: looks like egress path from nodes is dropping/blackholing. AWS health doesn't show AZ-wide event yet.
ken: checking NAT gateway and route table metrics. NAT gw in us-west-2a shows intermittent high active flows and 5xx from LB.
ranjit: ENI tx/err counters increasing on a subset of hosts: `ifconfig enx*` shows tx_queue_len growth and tx_dropped spikes. suspect host network driver qdisc saturation or hardware offload flapping.
emily: impact: Hosted inference REST and streaming RPCs from customers routed to us-west-2a have ~10-20% failure rate and increased tail latency. Dedicated customers pinned to that AZ are affected.
maria: immediate mitigation options: 1) shift traffic away from us-west-2a by updating service routing policy (fail open to cross-az), 2) cordon/drain worst nodes, 3) spin up replacement instances in us-west-2b and failover.
ken: rolling routing change is fast. I can flip route weight for region policy to prefer us-west-2b as standby. recommend incremental 20% steps to avoid overload.
emily: do it. flip +20% now and watch.
oncall-bot: user emily initiated route-weight-update (change_id: rw-8342) -> prefer us-west-2b +20%.
maria: observing success: 20% of affected requests now routed to 2b, error rate drops to ~9% overall.
ranjit: I'll start cordoning top 6 hosts with highest tx_drops. `kubectl cordon node-ux-1` then drain.
dan: while draining, some in-flight streams will fail. we should enable retry/backoff in our edge LB for 503->retry to other AZ. ops-bot: creating tempLB rule: edge-retry=3.
emily: ops-bot confirmed edge-retry applied. we may see duplicate tokens for streaming clients; inform SRE.
ken: also enabling cross-AZ burst capacity: launching 4 g5 instances in us-west-2b (type g5.xlarge) as warm capacity. will attach to infer pool.
emily: note to support: prepare customer message for impacted tenants: estimated 6-30m mitigation window, degraded success rate until traffic fully moved.
maria: creating a short status blip for status.redwood.ai -> "Partial egress packet loss affecting inference in us-west-2a, traffic being shifted to us-west-2b. Some requests may fail or be delayed."
ranjit: investigating root cause -> kernel driver logs show repeated offload reset: `mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: Reset adapter`. NIC firmware chatter. seems like host NIC offload resetting under specific tx load.
emily: that's helpful. plan: keep routing shift and drain affected hosts; don't reboot whole AZ. coordinate with SRE to file AWS support ticket for NIC firmware and capacity fallback.
ken: AWS support ticket opened (case #12345678) with packet captures attached. also requested NAT gateway internal metrics.
dan: rolling drains started. draining node-ux-1 -> pods moving to other AZs. expecting some 503s for streams.
maria: customer impact estimate: ~8 dedicated customers pinned to us-west-2a affected (20-80% of their traffic depending on routing). Hosted customers: roughly 14k requests/min with 5xx elevated for ~10% of traffic before routing change.
emily: timeline update for status page and internal: 03:13 UTC detection -> 03:18 UTC routing shift start -> 03:22 UTC initial error drop -> 03:29 UTC node drains started.
oncall-bot: emily is handing off to ken for next 2h rotation. ken: taking on-call.
ken: will keep route shift until drains complete and TX errors stop. also running a canary load to ensure us-west-2b kernel/NICs handle extra load.
ranjit: action items: 1) finish drains of affected hosts (in progress), 2) monitor 5xx and latency per-AZ, 3) finish replacement instances and de-register problematic hosts, 4) AWS support engagement on NIC resets, 5) postmortem once stable.
emily: @support-team please prepare outbound comms for enterprise customers pinned to ASG infer-g5-usw2a. include mitigation steps we took and ETA for full restoration.
ken: status @03:36 UTC -> global 5xx reduced to 2.1%, us-west-2a still at 6% but trending down. continuing monitoring.
ranjit: extra note: KV cache hits unaffected for cross-AZ requests but streaming retries cause some double-downloads; counting for billing team.
maria: if NIC firmware is root cause, we should add a health probe for tx_drop rate and auto-drain before heavy QPS to avoid noisy neighbor. filing infra ticket.
emily: good. logging final: leaning to close incident once us-west-2a 5xx <1% and all drained hosts reprovisioned. handoff complete.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place, on-call: ken until 05:36 UTC. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC.
